meaning.en: A departure from what is usual or expected.
meaning.ko: 일반적이거나 예상되는 상태에서 벗어난 현상.

example.text: The sudden rise in temperature was an aberration in an otherwise stable record.
example.en: The sudden rise in temperature was an aberration in an otherwise stable record.
example.ko: 그 밖에는 안정적이던 기록에서 갑작스러운 기온 상승은 이례적인 현상이었다.

meaning.en: Difficult to understand because the ideas are complex or specialised.
meaning.ko: 생각이나 내용이 복잡하거나 전문적이어서 이해하기 어려운.

example.text: The lecturer used a diagram to explain the abstruse theory.
example.en: The lecturer used a diagram to explain the abstruse theory.
example.ko: 강사는 난해한 이론을 설명하기 위해 도표를 사용했다.

meaning.en: Sharp and harsh in speech or tone, often with bitter humour.
meaning.ko: 말이나 어조가 날카롭고 신랄한, 흔히 씁쓸한 유머가 담긴.

example.text: Her acerbic review exposed the contradictions in his argument.
example.en: Her acerbic review exposed the contradictions in his argument.
example.ko: 그녀의 신랄한 비평은 그의 주장의 모순을 드러냈다.

meaning.en: To make a bad situation or condition less severe.
meaning.ko: 나쁜 상황이나 상태를 개선하거나 그 심각성을 줄이다.

example.text: The new drainage system should ameliorate the flooding problem.
example.en: The new drainage system should ameliorate the flooding problem.
example.ko: 새 배수 시설은 침수 문제를 완화할 것으로 기대된다.

meaning.en: Something associated with a different historical period from the one in which it appears.
meaning.ko: 등장한 시대와 다른 시대에 속하는 사물이나 관습 등.

example.text: The wristwatch in the medieval scene was an obvious anachronism.
example.en: The wristwatch in the medieval scene was an obvious anachronism.
example.ko: 중세 장면에 등장한 손목시계는 명백히 시대에 맞지 않는 물건이었다.

meaning.en: The exact opposite of an idea, quality or thing.
meaning.ko: 어떤 생각이나 특성 또는 사물과 정반대되는 것.

example.text: Her measured response was the antithesis of his angry outburst.
example.en: Her measured response was the antithesis of his angry outburst.
example.ko: 그녀의 신중한 반응은 그의 격한 분노 표출과 정반대였다.

meaning.en: Changing suddenly and unpredictably, often according to passing wishes.
meaning.ko: 흔히 순간적인 기분이나 욕구에 따라 갑작스럽고 예측하기 어렵게 바뀌는.

example.text: The capricious ruler reversed the decision the following morning.
example.en: The capricious ruler reversed the decision the following morning.
example.ko: 변덕스러운 통치자는 다음 날 아침 그 결정을 뒤집었다.

meaning.en: Clear, logical and convincing, especially of an argument or explanation.
meaning.ko: 특히 주장이나 설명이 명확하고 논리적이며 설득력 있는.

example.text: She presented a cogent argument for preserving the public archive.
example.en: She presented a cogent argument for preserving the public archive.
example.ko: 그녀는 공공 기록 보관소를 보존해야 한다는 설득력 있는 논거를 제시했다.

meaning.en: Causing harm or damage.
meaning.ko: 해롭거나 손상을 일으키는.

example.text: The study examined the deleterious effects of prolonged exposure to the chemical.
example.en: The study examined the deleterious effects of prolonged exposure to the chemical.
example.ko: 그 연구는 해당 화학 물질에 장기간 노출될 때 나타나는 유해한 영향을 조사했다.

meaning.en: Not fully honest or sincere, often while pretending to know less than one does.
meaning.ko: 흔히 실제보다 덜 아는 척하면서 솔직하거나 진실하지 않은.

example.text: It would be disingenuous to claim that no one had warned us about the risk.
example.en: It would be disingenuous to claim that no one had warned us about the risk.
example.ko: 아무도 그 위험을 경고하지 않았다고 주장한다면 솔직하지 못한 태도일 것이다.

meaning.en: To weaken someone or deprive them of energy.
meaning.ko: 누군가를 약하게 하거나 기력을 빼앗다.

example.text: Days of oppressive heat can enervate even experienced workers.
example.en: Days of oppressive heat can enervate even experienced workers.
example.ko: 숨 막히는 더위가 며칠씩 이어지면 숙련된 노동자조차 기력이 떨어질 수 있다.

meaning.en: Open to different interpretations and therefore unclear or uncertain.
meaning.ko: 여러 해석이 가능하여 뜻이나 판단이 분명하지 않은.

example.text: The evidence remains equivocal, so the committee has postponed its decision.
example.en: The evidence remains equivocal, so the committee has postponed its decision.
example.ko: 증거가 여전히 불분명해서 위원회는 결정을 미뤘다.

meaning.en: Understood by or intended for a small group with specialised knowledge.
meaning.ko: 전문 지식을 갖춘 소수만 이해하거나 그런 사람들을 대상으로 하는.

example.text: The essay explores an esoteric debate within medieval philosophy.
example.en: The essay explores an esoteric debate within medieval philosophy.
example.ko: 그 글은 중세 철학 분야의 전문가들만 이해할 만한 논쟁을 다룬다.

meaning.en: To clear someone of blame or show that they are not guilty.
meaning.ko: 누군가에게 책임이 없거나 죄가 없음을 밝히다.

example.text: The new evidence may exculpate the engineer blamed for the failure.
example.en: The new evidence may exculpate the engineer blamed for the failure.
example.ko: 새로운 증거는 고장의 책임자로 지목된 기술자에게 책임이 없음을 밝힐 수도 있다.

meaning.en: Only beginning to develop and not yet clearly formed or organised.
meaning.ko: 막 발달하기 시작하여 형태나 체계가 아직 분명하지 않은.

example.text: The proposal grew from an inchoate idea into a detailed research plan.
example.en: The proposal grew from an inchoate idea into a detailed research plan.
example.ko: 그 제안은 아직 구체화되지 않은 생각에서 상세한 연구 계획으로 발전했다.

meaning.en: Unwilling to change a position or make a compromise.
meaning.ko: 자신의 입장을 바꾸거나 타협하려 하지 않는.

example.text: The negotiators remained intransigent despite the growing cost of the dispute.
example.en: The negotiators remained intransigent despite the growing cost of the dispute.
example.ko: 분쟁으로 인한 비용이 계속 늘어났지만 협상 대표들은 타협하지 않았다.

meaning.en: To make something harder to understand, often deliberately.
meaning.ko: 흔히 의도적으로 어떤 내용을 더 이해하기 어렵게 만들다.

example.text: Technical jargon can obfuscate a simple explanation.
example.en: Technical jargon can obfuscate a simple explanation.
example.ko: 전문 용어는 간단한 설명도 이해하기 어렵게 만들 수 있다.

meaning.en: Excessively unwilling to spend money or use resources.
meaning.ko: 돈이나 자원을 쓰는 것을 지나치게 아끼는.

example.text: The parsimonious owner refused to replace the broken chairs.
example.en: The parsimonious owner refused to replace the broken chairs.
example.ko: 지나치게 인색한 주인은 망가진 의자를 교체하기를 거부했다.

meaning.en: Done routinely with little care, effort or interest.
meaning.ko: 관심이나 정성을 거의 기울이지 않고 형식적으로 하는.

example.text: After a perfunctory inspection, the official signed the form.
example.en: After a perfunctory inspection, the official signed the form.
example.ko: 담당자는 형식적인 점검을 마친 뒤 서류에 서명했다.

meaning.en: Stubbornly unwilling to follow instructions or accept control.
meaning.ko: 지시를 따르거나 통제를 받아들이기를 완강히 거부하는.

example.text: The recalcitrant witness refused to answer even the simplest questions.
example.en: The recalcitrant witness refused to answer even the simplest questions.
example.ko: 완강하게 저항하던 증인은 가장 간단한 질문에도 답하기를 거부했다.

meaning.en: To formally give up a belief, practice or allegiance and declare that one no longer accepts it.
meaning.ko: 신념이나 관행, 충성을 더 이상 받아들이지 않겠다고 공식적으로 선언하며 버리다.

example.text: The leader promised to abjure violence and pursue reform through elections.
example.en: The leader promised to abjure violence and pursue reform through elections.
example.ko: 그 지도자는 폭력을 버리고 선거를 통해 개혁을 추진하겠다고 약속했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal renunciation, stronger and more deliberate than simply stopping.

meaning.en: To leave secretly, especially to escape responsibility or the authorities.
meaning.ko: 특히 책임이나 당국을 피하려고 몰래 달아나다.

example.text: The suspect tried to abscond before the police arrived.
example.en: The suspect tried to abscond before the police arrived.
example.ko: 용의자는 경찰이 도착하기 전에 몰래 달아나려고 했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal legal-context verb for covert flight.

meaning.en: Growth produced by small additions accumulating over time.
meaning.ko: 작은 부분들이 시간이 지나면서 쌓여 생기는 증가나 성장.

example.text: The island grew through the gradual accretion of sand.
example.en: The island grew through the gradual accretion of sand.
example.ko: 그 섬은 모래가 서서히 쌓이면서 커졌다.

entries.difficultyReason: Process concept distinguishing cumulative growth from sudden expansion.

meaning.en: Bitterness and hostility expressed between people.
meaning.ko: 사람들 사이에서 드러나는 신랄한 적대감과 험악함.

example.text: The negotiations ended in acrimony after both sides rejected the compromise.
example.en: The negotiations ended in acrimony after both sides rejected the compromise.
example.ko: 양측이 타협안을 거부한 뒤 협상은 험악한 분위기 속에서 끝났다.

entries.difficultyReason: Nuanced interpersonal hostility, especially in argument.

meaning.en: To suggest the main shape of an idea without explaining it fully.
meaning.ko: 생각의 큰 윤곽을 자세히 설명하지 않고 대략 제시하다.

example.text: The introduction will adumbrate the argument developed in later chapters.
example.en: The introduction will adumbrate the argument developed in later chapters.
example.ko: 서론은 뒤의 장들에서 전개할 논지의 윤곽을 대략 제시할 것이다.

entries.difficultyReason: Scholarly verb for preliminary, incomplete exposition.

meaning.en: An eager readiness to respond or take action.
meaning.ko: 기꺼이 즉시 응하거나 행동하려는 적극적인 태도.

example.text: She accepted the unexpected assignment with alacrity.
example.en: She accepted the unexpected assignment with alacrity.
example.ko: 그녀는 뜻밖의 업무를 기꺼이 선뜻 맡았다.

entries.difficultyReason: Combines willingness with promptness rather than speed alone.

meaning.en: So mild and uncontroversial that it is unlikely to upset anyone.
meaning.ko: 너무 무난하고 논쟁의 여지가 없어 누구도 불편하게 하지 않을 만한.

example.text: The report offered an anodyne summary that avoided every disputed issue.
example.en: The report offered an anodyne summary that avoided every disputed issue.
example.ko: 그 보고서는 논쟁이 되는 쟁점을 모두 피한 무난한 요약을 제시했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Figurative evaluative sense of bland harmlessness.

meaning.en: Widely repeated although there is reason to doubt whether it is true.
meaning.ko: 널리 전해지지만 사실인지 의심할 만한 근거가 있는.

example.text: The guide admitted that the amusing story was probably apocryphal.
example.en: The guide admitted that the amusing story was probably apocryphal.
example.ko: 안내원은 그 재미있는 이야기가 아마 사실이 아닐 것이라고 인정했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Epistemic judgement separating a familiar story from verified history.

meaning.en: Someone who abandons a religion they previously followed.
meaning.ko: 전에 믿던 종교를 버린 사람; 배교자.

example.text: His former religious community regarded him as an apostate.
example.en: His former religious community regarded him as an apostate.
example.ko: 그가 속했던 종교 공동체는 그를 배교자로 여겼다.

entries.difficultyReason: Precise religious identity following renunciation.

meaning.en: Approval or praise given because something is judged worthy.
meaning.ko: 가치 있다고 판단하여 보내는 승인이나 칭찬.

example.text: The proposal won the committee's approbation after a thorough review.
example.en: The proposal won the committee's approbation after a thorough review.
example.ko: 그 제안은 철저한 검토 끝에 위원회의 승인을 얻었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal register of favourable judgement or sanction.

meaning.en: A damaging allegation or insinuation about someone's character.
meaning.ko: 다른 사람의 인격을 해치는 비난이나 암시.

example.text: She rejected the aspersion that her findings had been bought.
example.en: She rejected the aspersion that her findings had been bought.
example.ko: 그녀는 자신의 연구 결과가 돈에 매수되었다는 비난을 일축했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Rhetorical reputational attack, often indirect.

meaning.en: Giving steady, careful effort to a task over time.
meaning.ko: 일에 오랫동안 꾸준하고 세심하게 힘쓰는; 근면한.

example.text: His assiduous checking uncovered several errors in the archive.
example.en: His assiduous checking uncovered several errors in the archive.
example.ko: 그가 꾸준히 꼼꼼하게 확인한 덕분에 기록 보관 자료에서 여러 오류가 발견되었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Sustained diligence with attentive care.

meaning.en: A decrease in the strength or intensity of something.
meaning.ko: 무엇의 세기나 강도가 줄어드는 것; 감쇠.

example.text: The thick walls caused substantial attenuation of the radio signal.
example.en: The thick walls caused substantial attenuation of the radio signal.
example.ko: 두꺼운 벽 때문에 무선 신호의 세기가 크게 줄었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Abstract reduction in intensity, especially in technical analysis.

meaning.en: Willing to attempt something strikingly bold despite serious risks.
meaning.ko: 큰 위험에도 불구하고 눈에 띄게 대담한 일을 시도하려는.

example.text: It was an audacious plan to open a theatre in the abandoned station.
example.en: It was an audacious plan to open a theatre in the abandoned station.
example.ko: 버려진 역에 극장을 열겠다는 것은 대담한 계획이었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Evaluative boldness extending towards recklessness.

meaning.en: A powerful desire to acquire more wealth than one needs.
meaning.ko: 필요 이상으로 재물을 얻으려는 강한 욕심; 탐욕.

example.text: The novel shows how avarice destroys the merchant's friendships.
example.en: The novel shows how avarice destroys the merchant's friendships.
example.ko: 그 소설은 재물에 대한 탐욕이 상인의 우정을 어떻게 무너뜨리는지 보여 준다.

entries.difficultyReason: Moral abstraction of excessive acquisitiveness.

meaning.en: Inclined to threaten, quarrel or seek conflict.
meaning.ko: 위협하거나 다투거나 충돌을 일으키려는 성향이 있는; 호전적인.

example.text: The ambassador's bellicose remarks made a peaceful settlement harder.
example.en: The ambassador's bellicose remarks made a peaceful settlement harder.
example.ko: 대사의 호전적인 발언으로 평화적인 해결이 더 어려워졌다.

entries.difficultyReason: Disposition towards aggressive confrontation.

meaning.en: Actively doing good or providing help to others.
meaning.ko: 다른 사람에게 적극적으로 선행을 베풀거나 도움을 주는.

example.text: The charity described its work as a beneficent influence on the town.
example.en: The charity described its work as a beneficent influence on the town.
example.ko: 그 자선 단체는 자신의 활동이 마을에 좋은 영향을 준다고 설명했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal moral evaluation emphasising helpful action.

meaning.en: Flattery or an enticing gesture intended to win someone's agreement.
meaning.ko: 상대의 동의를 얻으려고 하는 아첨이나 환심을 사는 행동.

example.text: He recognised the generous compliment as a blandishment rather than honest praise.
example.en: He recognised the generous compliment as a blandishment rather than honest praise.
example.ko: 그는 그 후한 칭찬이 솔직한 찬사가 아니라 환심을 사려는 아첨임을 알아차렸다.

entries.difficultyReason: Persuasive flattery with an instrumental motive.

meaning.en: Using inflated, impressive-sounding language that exceeds the substance of what is said.
meaning.ko: 내용에 비해 지나치게 거창하고 과장된 말을 쓰는.

example.text: The editor replaced the bombastic opening with a clear statement of the facts.
example.en: The editor replaced the bombastic opening with a clear statement of the facts.
example.ko: 편집자는 과장되고 거창한 도입부를 사실을 명확하게 밝히는 문장으로 바꾸었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Rhetorical criticism of inflated expression.

meaning.en: So complicated and full of interconnected rules or details that it is difficult to follow.
meaning.ko: 규칙이나 세부 사항이 복잡하게 얽혀 이해하거나 따르기 어려운.

example.text: Applicants struggled to navigate the byzantine appeals procedure.
example.en: Applicants struggled to navigate the byzantine appeals procedure.
example.ko: 신청자들은 복잡하게 얽힌 이의 신청 절차를 따라가는 데 애를 먹었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Figurative description of obstructive institutional complexity.

meaning.en: A harsh mixture of sounds that clash with one another.
meaning.ko: 서로 어울리지 않는 소리가 뒤섞인 거슬리는 소음.

example.text: A cacophony of alarms filled the control room.
example.en: A cacophony of alarms filled the control room.
example.ko: 여러 경보음이 뒤섞인 시끄러운 소리가 제어실을 가득 채웠다.

entries.difficultyReason: Aesthetic judgement of discordant sound rather than simple loudness.

meaning.en: A knowingly false claim intended to damage another person's reputation.
meaning.ko: 다른 사람의 평판을 해치려고 고의로 하는 거짓 주장; 중상모략.

example.text: The accusation was exposed as calumny when the original records were found.
example.en: The accusation was exposed as calumny when the original records were found.
example.ko: 원본 기록이 발견되자 그 비난은 중상모략으로 드러났다.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal moral and reputational concept of malicious falsehood.

meaning.en: Dishonest manoeuvring that uses technicalities or tricks to gain an advantage.
meaning.ko: 유리한 결과를 얻으려고 형식적인 구실이나 속임수를 쓰는 부정한 책략.

example.text: The audit uncovered financial chicanery concealed behind complicated contracts.
example.en: The audit uncovered financial chicanery concealed behind complicated contracts.
example.ko: 감사에서 복잡한 계약 뒤에 숨겨진 금융상의 부정한 책략이 드러났다.

entries.difficultyReason: Deception through manipulative procedural or verbal tactics.

meaning.en: An indirect, wordy way of expressing something that could be stated more simply.
meaning.ko: 더 간단히 말할 수 있는 내용을 장황하게 돌려 말하는 방식.

example.text: After several minutes of circumlocution, he finally admitted that the money was gone.
example.en: After several minutes of circumlocution, he finally admitted that the money was gone.
example.ko: 몇 분 동안 말을 빙빙 돌린 끝에 그는 마침내 돈이 없어졌다고 인정했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Rhetorical indirection that adds unnecessary wording.

meaning.en: Matching something else appropriately in scale, value or degree.
meaning.ko: 규모나 가치, 정도가 다른 것에 알맞게 상응하는.

example.text: The payment should be commensurate with the responsibility involved.
example.en: The payment should be commensurate with the responsibility involved.
example.ko: 보수는 맡는 책임에 상응해야 한다.

entries.difficultyReason: Proportional relation rather than mere equality.

meaning.en: Readily accommodating other people's wishes, sometimes too readily.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal relation of co-occurrence without necessarily claiming causation.

entries.difficultyReason: Qualified refusal or hesitation, often in formal exchanges.

entries.difficultyReason: Pragmatic mismatch between levity and required seriousness.

meaning.en: Occurring by chance rather than through deliberate planning.
meaning.ko: 의도적으로 계획해서가 아니라 우연히 일어난.

example.text: A fortuitous meeting at the station led to their research partnership.
example.en: A fortuitous meeting at the station led to their research partnership.
example.ko: 역에서의 우연한 만남이 두 사람의 공동 연구로 이어졌다.

entries.difficultyReason: Accidental origin; fortunate outcomes are possible but not required.

meaning.en: To express fierce condemnation in speech or writing.
meaning.ko: 말이나 글로 격렬하게 비난하다.

example.text: The columnist continued to fulminate against the proposed restrictions.
example.en: The columnist continued to fulminate against the proposed restrictions.
example.ko: 그 칼럼니스트는 제안된 제한 조치를 계속 격렬하게 비난했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Emphatic rhetorical denunciation, commonly followed by 'against'.

meaning.en: Talking at tiresome length, often about unimportant details.
meaning.ko: 대개 중요하지 않은 세부 사항을 지칠 만큼 길게 떠드는.

example.text: Our garrulous guide spent half an hour describing his breakfast.
example.en: Our garrulous guide spent half an hour describing his breakfast.
example.ko: 말이 지나치게 많은 안내원은 자신의 아침 식사를 설명하는 데 삼십 분을 썼다.

entries.difficultyReason: Negative evaluation of excessive, tedious speech.

meaning.en: Using exaggeratedly impressive language to display importance.
meaning.ko: 중요해 보이려고 지나치게 거창한 표현을 쓰는.

example.text: The grandiloquent announcement promised a revolution but described only minor changes.
example.en: The grandiloquent announcement promised a revolution but described only minor changes.
example.ko: 거창한 그 발표는 혁명을 약속했지만 사소한 변화만 설명했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Ostentatious verbal style disproportionate to substance.

meaning.en: Open and honest, without an intention to deceive.
meaning.ko: 속일 의도 없이 솔직하고 순진한.

example.text: His guileless answer made it clear that he knew nothing of the scheme.
example.en: His guileless answer made it clear that he knew nothing of the scheme.
example.ko: 그의 솔직하고 순진한 대답은 그가 그 계략을 전혀 몰랐음을 분명히 보여 주었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Absence of deception, sometimes accompanied by naivety.

meaning.en: Used so frequently that it no longer feels fresh or effective.
meaning.ko: 너무 자주 쓰여 참신함이나 효과가 사라진; 진부한.

example.text: The speech relied on hackneyed phrases instead of concrete proposals.
example.en: The speech relied on hackneyed phrases instead of concrete proposals.
example.ko: 그 연설은 구체적인 제안 대신 진부한 문구에 의존했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Literary evaluation of originality lost through repetition.

meaning.en: Someone who challenges beliefs or conventions that others treat as beyond question.
meaning.ko: 다른 사람들이 당연하게 받아들이는 신념이나 관습에 도전하는 사람.

example.text: The architect gained a reputation as an iconoclast for rejecting fashionable styles.
example.en: The architect gained a reputation as an iconoclast for rejecting fashionable styles.
example.ko: 그 건축가는 유행하는 양식을 거부하여 기존 관습에 도전하는 사람으로 명성을 얻었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Figurative opposition to revered intellectual or cultural norms.

meaning.en: Unable to be soothed or persuaded to abandon hostility.
meaning.ko: 달래거나 설득해도 적대감을 거두지 않는; 누그러뜨릴 수 없는.

example.text: Even after the apology, she remained an implacable opponent of the plan.
example.en: Even after the apology, she remained an implacable opponent of the plan.
example.ko: 사과를 받은 뒤에도 그녀는 그 계획에 대한 완강한 반대자로 남았다.

entries.difficultyReason: Persistent hostility resistant to reconciliation.

meaning.en: To challenge the honesty, validity or legitimacy of something.
meaning.ko: 정직성이나 타당성, 정당성에 의문을 제기하다.

example.text: The lawyer sought to impugn the reliability of the witness's account.
example.en: The lawyer sought to impugn the reliability of the witness's account.
example.ko: 변호사는 증인의 진술이 믿을 만한지 의문을 제기하려 했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal argumentative attack on credibility or validity.

meaning.en: Impossible to escape or prevent.
meaning.ko: 벗어나거나 막을 수 없는; 피할 수 없는.

example.text: The narrator treats ageing as an ineluctable part of life.
example.en: The narrator treats ageing as an ineluctable part of life.
example.ko: 화자는 나이 드는 일을 삶의 피할 수 없는 일부로 다룬다.

entries.difficultyReason: Elevated philosophical sense of unavoidable necessity.

meaning.en: Too profound or intense to be expressed adequately in words.
meaning.ko: 너무 깊거나 강렬하여 말로 충분히 표현할 수 없는.

example.text: She described an ineffable sense of peace on returning home.
example.en: She described an ineffable sense of peace on returning home.
example.ko: 그녀는 집으로 돌아왔을 때 말로 다 표현할 수 없는 평온함을 느꼈다고 했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Limits of verbal expression for an experience or quality.

meaning.en: Sincere and unguarded, sometimes because of limited experience.
meaning.ko: 솔직하고 경계심이 없으며 때로는 경험이 부족해 순진한.

example.text: His ingenuous question exposed a flaw that the experts had overlooked.
example.en: His ingenuous question exposed a flaw that the experts had overlooked.
example.ko: 그의 순진하고 솔직한 질문이 전문가들이 놓친 결함을 드러냈다.

entries.difficultyReason: Uncontrived sincerity; distinct from inventive 'ingenious'.

meaning.en: Working against someone's interests or making a desirable outcome harder.
meaning.ko: 누군가의 이익에 해롭거나 바람직한 결과를 어렵게 하는.

example.text: Secrecy is inimical to the public trust the agency hopes to build.
example.en: Secrecy is inimical to the public trust the agency hopes to build.
example.ko: 비밀주의는 그 기관이 쌓으려는 대중의 신뢰에 해롭다.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal adverse relationship, typically expressed with 'to'.

meaning.en: Lacking the character or interest needed to make an impression.
meaning.ko: 특색이나 흥미가 없어 별다른 인상을 주지 못하는; 재미없는.

example.text: The adaptation turned a lively novel into an insipid drama.
example.en: The adaptation turned a lively novel into an insipid drama.
example.ko: 그 각색은 생기 넘치는 소설을 특색 없는 드라마로 바꾸어 놓았다.

entries.difficultyReason: Figurative aesthetic blandness rather than literal taste.

meaning.en: Showing a relaxed lack of concern, even when concern might be expected.
meaning.ko: 걱정할 만한 상황에서도 느긋하게 무심한 태도를 보이는.

example.text: His insouciant response irritated colleagues who were worried about the deadline.
example.en: His insouciant response irritated colleagues who were worried about the deadline.
example.ko: 마감일을 걱정하던 동료들은 그의 태평한 반응에 짜증이 났다.

entries.difficultyReason: Nuanced carefree attitude that may imply inappropriate indifference.

meaning.en: Having a firmly established habit that has continued for a long time.
meaning.ko: 오랫동안 계속된 습관이 굳게 자리 잡은; 상습적인.

example.text: An inveterate collector, she found it difficult to throw away old tickets.
example.en: An inveterate collector, she found it difficult to throw away old tickets.
example.ko: 수집하는 습관이 깊이 밴 그녀는 오래된 표를 버리기 어려워했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Entrenched personal habit rather than temporary behaviour.

meaning.en: Quick to become angry over relatively small provocations.
meaning.ko: 비교적 사소한 자극에도 쉽게 화를 내는; 성마른.

example.text: The irascible landlord snapped at anyone who rang the wrong bell.
example.en: The irascible landlord snapped at anyone who rang the wrong bell.
example.ko: 성마른 집주인은 벨을 잘못 누르는 사람마다 버럭 화를 냈다.

entries.difficultyReason: Temperamental susceptibility to anger.

meaning.en: Expressing a message in very few words.
meaning.ko: 아주 적은 말로 뜻을 전달하는; 간결한.

example.text: His laconic reply gave us the answer but no explanation.
example.en: His laconic reply gave us the answer but no explanation.
example.ko: 그의 간결한 답변은 답은 알려 주었지만 설명은 해 주지 않았다.

entries.difficultyReason: Economy of expression as a distinctive communicative style.

meaning.en: A state of weariness in which energy and motivation are reduced.
meaning.ko: 기력과 의욕이 떨어지는 피로하고 나른한 상태.

example.text: After weeks of illness, she struggled with persistent lassitude.
example.en: After weeks of illness, she struggled with persistent lassitude.
example.ko: 몇 주 동안 앓고 난 뒤 그녀는 계속되는 무기력과 피로에 시달렸다.

entries.difficultyReason: Sustained low energy with diminished inclination to act.

meaning.en: Expressing approval and admiration for someone or something.
meaning.ko: 누군가나 무엇에 대한 찬성과 감탄을 표현하는; 칭찬하는.

example.text: The book received a laudatory review in the literary journal.
example.en: The book received a laudatory review in the literary journal.
example.ko: 그 책은 문학 잡지에서 찬사를 담은 서평을 받았다.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal description of praise-bearing commentary.

meaning.en: Inclined to talk freely and at length.
meaning.ko: 말을 거리낌 없이 많이 하는 성향의; 수다스러운.

example.text: The usually loquacious host fell silent when the results appeared.
example.en: The usually loquacious host fell silent when the results appeared.
example.ko: 평소 수다스러운 진행자는 결과가 나오자 말을 멈추었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Elevated description of a talkative disposition.

meaning.en: Marked by deep or exaggerated gloom and mournfulness.
meaning.ko: 깊거나 과장된 우울함과 슬픔이 드러나는.

example.text: The actor gave the trivial complaint a deliberately lugubrious tone.
example.en: The actor gave the trivial complaint a deliberately lugubrious tone.
example.ko: 배우는 사소한 불평에 일부러 지나치게 비통한 어조를 실었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Literary mood description often suggesting excessive melancholy.

meaning.en: Generous and free from petty resentment, especially towards a rival or someone less powerful.
meaning.ko: 특히 경쟁자나 약자에게 너그럽고 사소한 원한을 품지 않는; 도량이 큰.

example.text: The winner was magnanimous towards the rival who had criticised her.
example.en: The winner was magnanimous towards the rival who had criticised her.
example.ko: 우승자는 자신을 비판했던 경쟁자에게도 너그럽게 대했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Moral generosity expressed where vindictiveness would be possible.

meaning.en: Deliberately saying or presenting what is untrue.
meaning.ko: 일부러 사실이 아닌 것을 말하거나 제시하는; 거짓말을 하는.

example.text: The inquiry exposed the mendacious claim that all residents had been consulted.
example.en: The inquiry exposed the mendacious claim that all residents had been consulted.
example.ko: 조사에서 모든 주민의 의견을 들었다는 주장이 고의적인 거짓임이 드러났다.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal judgement of intentional untruthfulness.

meaning.en: Changing quickly and unpredictably in mood or behaviour.
meaning.ko: 기분이나 행동이 빠르고 예측하기 어렵게 바뀌는.

example.text: The mercurial director praised the design in the morning and rejected it by lunch.
example.en: The mercurial director praised the design in the morning and rejected it by lunch.
example.ko: 변덕스러운 감독은 아침에는 그 디자인을 칭찬했다가 점심때가 되자 거절했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Temperamental volatility rather than ordinary change.

meaning.en: Giving money or other help on an exceptionally generous scale.
meaning.ko: 돈이나 다른 도움을 매우 후하게 베푸는.

example.text: A munificent donation allowed the library to reopen its children's room.
example.en: A munificent donation allowed the library to reopen its children's room.
example.ko: 매우 후한 기부 덕분에 도서관은 어린이실을 다시 열 수 있었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal praise for unusually lavish generosity.

meaning.en: Only beginning to exist or develop.
meaning.ko: 이제 막 생겨나거나 발전하기 시작한; 초기 단계의.

example.text: The grant supported a nascent industry with few established investors.
example.en: The grant supported a nascent industry with few established investors.
example.ko: 그 보조금은 기반을 잡은 투자자가 거의 없는 초기 단계의 산업을 지원했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Emergence at an early developmental stage.

meaning.en: Deliberately and seriously wicked or criminal.
meaning.ko: 고의적이며 매우 사악하거나 범죄적인.

example.text: The investigation revealed a nefarious scheme to steal pension funds.
example.en: The investigation revealed a nefarious scheme to steal pension funds.
example.ko: 조사에서 연기금을 훔치려는 사악한 계획이 드러났다.

entries.difficultyReason: Strong moral condemnation of purposeful wrongdoing.

meaning.en: A person newly entering an activity, field or belief system.
meaning.ko: 활동이나 분야, 신앙 체계에 갓 들어온 사람; 초심자.

example.text: A neophyte in diplomacy, he relied heavily on his experienced advisers.
example.en: A neophyte in diplomacy, he relied heavily on his experienced advisers.
example.ko: 외교의 초심자였던 그는 경험 많은 참모들에게 크게 의존했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal novice term used in intellectual and institutional contexts.

meaning.en: Disgusting to the senses, especially because of a foul smell.
meaning.ko: 특히 악취 때문에 감각적으로 역겹거나 불쾌한.

example.text: A noisome smell rose from the stagnant water behind the warehouse.
example.en: A noisome smell rose from the stagnant water behind the warehouse.
example.ko: 창고 뒤에 고인 물에서 역겨운 악취가 올라왔다.

entries.difficultyReason: Literary sensory offensiveness, not related to loud noise.

meaning.en: Refusing to change one's position or behaviour despite strong reasons to do so.
meaning.ko: 바꿀 만한 충분한 이유가 있어도 입장이나 행동을 고집스럽게 바꾸지 않는.

example.text: The landlord remained obdurate despite repeated evidence that the charge was wrong.
example.en: The landlord remained obdurate despite repeated evidence that the charge was wrong.
example.ko: 요금이 잘못되었다는 증거가 거듭 제시되어도 집주인은 완강하게 입장을 바꾸지 않았다.

entries.difficultyReason: Moral or argumentative stubbornness resistant to correction.

meaning.en: Excessively eager to please or obey someone with greater power.
meaning.ko: 권력이 더 큰 사람을 기쁘게 하거나 따르려고 지나치게 비위를 맞추는.

example.text: His obsequious compliments made the visiting official uncomfortable.
example.en: His obsequious compliments made the visiting official uncomfortable.
example.ko: 그의 지나치게 아첨하는 칭찬은 방문한 관리자를 불편하게 했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Critical description of servile accommodation.

meaning.en: Noisily resisting control or refusing to cooperate.
meaning.ko: 시끄럽게 통제에 반항하거나 협조를 거부하는.

example.text: The obstreperous crowd repeatedly drowned out the speaker.
example.en: The obstreperous crowd repeatedly drowned out the speaker.
example.ko: 시끄럽게 반항하는 군중은 연설자의 말을 번번이 소음으로 묻어 버렸다.

entries.difficultyReason: Combines unruliness with disruptive resistance.

meaning.en: Deserving intense dislike because it is deeply offensive or objectionable.
meaning.ko: 매우 불쾌하거나 부당하여 강한 혐오를 불러일으키는.

example.text: She refused to defend the company's odious treatment of its workers.
example.en: She refused to defend the company's odious treatment of its workers.
example.ko: 그녀는 그 회사가 노동자들을 혐오스러울 만큼 부당하게 대한 일을 옹호하기를 거부했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Strong moral evaluation of something repellent.

meaning.en: Requiring so much effort or responsibility that it becomes burdensome.
meaning.ko: 노력이나 책임이 많이 필요하여 부담이 큰.

example.text: The agreement imposed onerous reporting duties on a small charity.
example.en: The agreement imposed onerous reporting duties on a small charity.
example.ko: 그 협정은 작은 자선 단체에 부담이 큰 보고 의무를 부과했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Burden arising from an obligation rather than physical weight alone.

meaning.en: Public contempt or disgrace resulting from conduct judged shameful.
meaning.ko: 수치스러운 행동으로 인해 받는 공개적인 경멸이나 불명예.

example.text: The scandal brought lasting opprobrium upon the former minister.
example.en: The scandal brought lasting opprobrium upon the former minister.
example.ko: 그 추문은 전직 장관에게 오래도록 불명예와 비난을 안겼다.

entries.difficultyReason: Social condemnation grounded in a moral judgement.

meaning.en: Designed to impress others through a conspicuous display of wealth or importance.
meaning.ko: 부나 중요성을 눈에 띄게 과시하여 남에게 인상을 주려는.

example.text: The office rejected ostentatious furnishings in favour of simple, durable desks.
example.en: The office rejected ostentatious furnishings in favour of simple, durable desks.
example.ko: 사무실은 과시적인 가구 대신 단순하고 튼튼한 책상을 택했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Intentional display aimed at attracting admiration.

meaning.en: To ease symptoms without necessarily removing their underlying cause.
meaning.ko: 근본 원인을 반드시 없애지는 않으면서 증상을 완화하다.

example.text: The treatment may palliate the pain without curing the disease.
example.en: The treatment may palliate the pain without curing the disease.
example.ko: 그 치료는 병을 낫게 하지는 못하더라도 통증을 완화할 수 있다.

entries.difficultyReason: Clinical distinction between relief and cure.

meaning.en: An amount or number too small to meet a need.
meaning.ko: 필요를 충족하기에는 너무 적은 양이나 수; 부족.

example.text: The paucity of reliable records limited the historian's conclusions.
example.en: The paucity of reliable records limited the historian's conclusions.
example.ko: 믿을 만한 기록이 부족하여 역사가가 내릴 수 있는 결론이 제한되었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Formal insufficiency of available material or evidence.

meaning.en: Giving excessive importance to minor rules or details of knowledge.
meaning.ko: 사소한 규칙이나 지식의 세부 사항을 지나치게 중요하게 여기는; 현학적인.

example.text: His pedantic objection concerned a comma rather than the substance of the argument.
example.en: His pedantic objection concerned a comma rather than the substance of the argument.
example.ko: 그의 현학적인 이의는 논지의 내용이 아니라 쉼표 하나에 관한 것이었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Misplaced intellectual precision at the expense of substance.

meaning.en: Expressing a negative or belittling judgement about someone or something.
meaning.ko: 누군가나 무엇을 부정적으로 평가하거나 깎아내리는 뜻을 담은.

example.text: The researchers avoided the pejorative label used in earlier reports.
example.en: The researchers avoided the pejorative label used in earlier reports.
example.ko: 연구자들은 이전 보고서에서 사용한 비하적인 명칭을 피했다.

entries.difficultyReason: Evaluative force carried by a word or expression.

meaning.en: Expressed with such clarity that it is readily understood.
meaning.ko: 표현이 매우 명료하여 쉽게 이해되는.

example.text: Her pellucid explanation made the difficult argument accessible.
example.en: Her pellucid explanation made the difficult argument accessible.
example.ko: 그녀의 명료한 설명 덕분에 어려운 논지를 이해할 수 있었다.

entries.difficultyReason: Elevated figurative clarity of exposition.

meaning.en: Unwilling to spend money even when spending would be reasonable.
meaning.ko: 돈을 써도 될 만한 상황에서도 쓰기를 꺼리는; 몹시 인색한.

example.text: The penurious owner refused to replace even the broken office kettle.
example.en: The penurious owner refused to replace even the broken office kettle.
example.ko: 몹시 인색한 주인은 고장 난 사무실 주전자조차 교체하지 않았다.

entries.difficultyReason: Miserly sense, distinguished from simply being poor.

meaning.en: Causing serious harm in a way that may be difficult to notice at first.
